title: Understanding the mind
description: How Indian traditions map the mind and train it, from the Gita's practice and dispassion to Sankhya's model, Patanjali's Yoga, Hatha Yoga's breath and body, and Buddhist meditation. It shows both shared techniques and different views of what lies beyond the mind.

steps.title: The mind is like the wind
steps.note: Arjuna voices the universal complaint: the mind is restless and stubborn.

steps.title: Practice and dispassion
steps.note: Krishna's answer names the two supports that Patanjali also uses.

steps.title: A lamp in a windless place
steps.note: The image of a steady, meditative mind.

steps.title: Sankhya's map
steps.note: Mind, intellect and ego belong to nature, not to consciousness.

steps.title: Buddhi, manas, ahankara
steps.note: The inner instrument in its parts.

steps.title: The 25 principles
steps.note: See where the mind sits among Sankhya's evolutes.

steps.title: Yoga Sutras
steps.note: Yoga as stilling the fluctuations of the mind-field.

steps.title: Chitta and its vrittis
steps.note: Five kinds of mental fluctuation and how they are quietened.

steps.title: Samadhi
steps.note: The stages of absorption described by Patanjali.

steps.title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
steps.note: Body, breath and energy as means of steadying the mind.

steps.title: Pranayama
steps.note: Breath regulation and its relation to mental steadiness.

steps.title: Buddhist approaches
steps.note: Mindfulness and insight that see mental events as impermanent and not-self.
